# Each desktop app's window opens its own view, loaded on first open

## Context

#21353 asks every web desktop app to open a working view, each loaded on its app's first open and sized for its content. Its intake on 2026-11-18 found that the route it prescribes does not exist yet, for two reasons:

- `Neo.desktop.Container` builds every window's config in its protected `getWindowConfig(record)`, so a consumer cannot give one app its own content or size without subclassing the container.
- A lazy item, `{module: () => import('...')}`, loads only in a card layout. In a window's body it stays parked and invisible.

This leaf adds the seam, and `examples/desktop/basic`'s three apps become its first consumer. #21353 then builds the demo's eleven apps on it.

## The Problem

- `src/desktop/Container.mjs:204`: `getWindowConfig(record)` returns the same keys for every app (the animate target, the boundary, the record and the browser window). Nothing in it varies per app.
- `src/container/Base.mjs:463-485`: an item whose `module` is a function is parked (`vdom.removeDom: true`). Only `layout.Card#loadModule` (`src/layout/Card.mjs:264`) loads one, when its card activates. `apps/form/view/FormContainer.mjs:66` works because its pages are cards.
- The example's three apps each show one sentence (`examples/desktop/basic/AppWindow.mjs`), and the demo's eleven all open the same `AppView` card.

## The Architectural Reality

- `Neo.desktop.WindowManager#createWindow` (`src/desktop/WindowManager.mjs:226`) awaits `#loadWindowClass()`, checks the open's ticket (`#admits`), and then calls `windowConfig?.(record)` synchronously. A rejected load rejects the open, and `openApp`'s `finally` (`:427-432`) clears the in-flight entry so the next open retries. A second open of the same app joins the first one's load.
- `Neo.desktop.Container#windowClass` already takes a class or a loader (`src/desktop/Container.mjs:116-122`), and an app's view fits the same shape.
- The window's `record` stays its only public input (#21198). Which view an app opens is the consumer's catalog knowledge.

Design authority: #21198, the window manager's intended shape: "one window per app id, created on first open through a configurable window class". #21353 AC-1: "Each view's module loads on its app's first open".

## The Fix

1. `Neo.desktop.Container#appWindowConfigs`: each app window's own config, keyed by app id. An entry takes any window config, such as `width` and `height`, plus `view`: the app's content, as a class or as a loader such as `() => import('./apps/Mail.mjs')`. `getWindowConfig(record)` becomes async, resolves `view`, and returns it as the window's one item, filling the window.
2. `Neo.desktop.WindowManager#createWindow` awaits the window config together with the window class, before the ticket check. An open that ends during either load creates no window, and a failed load lets the next open retry, as a failed class load does today.
3. In `examples/desktop/basic`, Notes edits a note in a `TextArea`, Calculator calculates, and Music lists its tracks in a grid, each at its own size. `examples/desktop/basic/AppWindow.mjs` and its CSS go.

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neo.desktop.Container#appWindowConfigs` (new) | #21198's shape, this ticket | each app window's own config by app id, with `view` as a class or loader resolved on the app's first open | an app without an entry opens the window class as it is | JSDoc; #21202's guide | unit arms |
| `Neo.desktop.WindowManager#windowConfig` | `src/desktop/WindowManager.mjs:61-66` | may return a Promise, awaited together with the window class before the ticket check | a config returned as an object works as today | JSDoc | unit arm: an open that ends during the load creates no window |
| `Neo.desktop.Container#getWindowConfig` (protected) | `src/desktop/Container.mjs:198-219` | async | a subclass that returns an object still works, since the manager awaits either | JSDoc | unit arm |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: An app with an `appWindowConfigs` entry opens at that size, with its `view` as the window's content. An app without an entry opens the window class as it is.
- [ ] AC-2: A loader `view` runs on its app's first open, not when the desktop is constructed, and a second open during the load creates no second window.
- [ ] AC-3: An open that ends during the view's load (a close, a reset or a destroy) creates no window, and a failed load lets the next open retry.
- [ ] AC-4: In `examples/desktop/basic`, a typed note is still there after the window closes and reopens, a sum computes, and the track list shows. Each window opens at its own size inside the workspace at 1440 × 900 and at 390 × 844.
- [ ] AC-5: `e2e/desktop/Basic.spec.mjs` and `unit/desktop/*` pass, and the example logs no console error.
- [ ] AC-6 (Look): before and after frames of the example with two apps open, and a cold look at the after frame.

## Out of Scope

The demo's eleven apps (#21353, which builds on this leaf), lazy items in layouts other than the card layout (an engine-wide change), and the tear-out (D#21204).

## Avoided Traps

- **A lazy item in the window's body:** only a card layout loads one.
- **A one-card card layout, borrowed for its lazy loading:** it works, but it reads as an accident.
- **A container subclass in each consumer** to override the protected `getWindowConfig`.
- **A window class per app** (#21353's trap): one window class, with one view per app.
- **The name `windowConfigs`:** `Neo.windowConfigs` already holds each browser window's config, and #21198's naming rule keeps "window" for the browser window unless the name says app window.
